LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 5.1.1 CONVERSATIONAL SKILLS – TONGUE TWISTERS AND RIDDLES

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.1: Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Conversational Skills – Tongue Twisters and Riddles
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Conversational Skills – Tongue Twisters and Riddles, part of Strand 5 in Grade 7 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why are tongue twisters important in language development? 2. How do riddles help in enhancing communication?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. take turns to perform common riddles,

2. work jointly to discuss the process of riddling,

3. practise turn-taking, negotiation and interjection as part of the riddling process,

4. brainstorm the features of a riddle,

5. compete with peers to say tongue twisters and record them,

6. listen to recorded audio clips of tongue twisters and peer review,

7. compose tongue twisters and take turns to perform them, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. take turns to perform common riddles,
2. work jointly to discuss the process of riddling,
3. practise turn-taking, negotiation and interjection as part of the riddling process,
4. brainstorm the features of a riddle,
5. compete with peers to say tongue twisters and record them,
6. listen to recorded audio clips of tongue twisters and peer review,
7. compose tongue twisters and take turns to perform them, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Conversational Skills – Tongue Twisters and Riddles together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and Problem-solving: This is developed as the learner follows simple instructions when performing

riddles and tongue twisters.

• Learning to Learn: This is realised as the learner works and engages in collective learning to compose and perform

tongue twisters.

Values:
• Unity: This is promoted as the learner cooperates with peers to take turns to perform riddles and tongue twisters.

• Respect: This is developed as the learner accommodates peers’ opinions as they compose tongue twisters.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Ethnic and racial relations is enhanced as the learner is exposed to riddles and tongue twisters from different communities

during performance and discussion.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the skills of performing riddles and tongue twisters to their learning in English and Kiswahili.
